positive_controls.argument: Architecture assumptions identify which behaviors and interactions need observation, connecting operational signals to a named feasibility question instead of collecting undirected telemetry.
The stated envelope and its assumptions identify meaningful monitoring conditions, anomaly thresholds and which changed operating state needs renewed evidence.
Hazard scenarios and control claims identify consequential signals and responsible recipients, concentrating observation and learning on risks that matter.
The transition plan identifies the operative people, procedures, support and contingency decisions that observations must inform and who can act on them.
Recovery objectives and known state/dependency models define which observations are necessary to detect failure, evaluate restoration and distinguish service availability from state integrity.
Support ownership, configuration history and retirement horizon identify the recipient, relevant fleet and feasible corrective actions for operational learning.
The explicit consequence and commitment model identifies which observations can discriminate a control decision and where information cost, privacy or delayed action defeats added instrumentation.
Rejecting the undifferentiated late-cost rule requires operational learning to retain distinct cost bearers and components instead of attributing every loss to the phase of discovery.
